hypothesis: H1a: a recalibration available in deployment repairs the ECE increase
test: temperature fitted on the in-pipeline validation stream, applied unchanged to L2
verdict: not supported: the residual ECE is still above the clean model's unscaled value

hypothesis: H1b: some monotone rescaling repairs it
test: temperature fitted on the target stream itself, which needs target labels and is unattainable in deployment
value: 0.129 -> 0.074; fitted temperature 1.24 on validation vs 2.25 on target
verdict: supported, but only with target labels: most of the excess is scale, and the scale correction cannot be learned in-pipeline

hypothesis: H1c: the augmented deficit is confined to probability scale and leaves ranking intact
test: ROC-AUC, invariant to any monotone rescaling
quantity: L2 ROC-AUC at window 160, clean vs augmented
verdict: not supported: augmentation degrades ranking as well as scale at this window

hypothesis: H2a: the deficit tracks how much of each message the window discards, within the corpus
test: augmentation contrast by untruncated message length at window 160
quantity: augmented-minus-clean L2 F1, shortest vs longest quartile
verdict: not corroborated, and this test has little power: the corpus is uniformly long, so every quartile loses a similar share

hypothesis: H2b: widening the window removes the deficit on the same messages
test: identical corpus and seeds refitted at window 320
quantity: augmented-minus-clean L2 F1 and ROC-AUC, 160 vs 320
verdict: supported: the ranking degradation is specific to the truncated window and reverses when the message is restored

hypothesis: H3: a badly placed decision threshold explains the deficit
test: target-oracle threshold applied to the same probabilities
quantity: L2 F1 at t=0.5 -> at the oracle threshold
verdict: not supported: both conditions gain a little and the ordering is unchanged
